idiom_name: opaque struct + order_* functions in one translation unit
implementation_notes: C has no access control, so the boundary is a convention held by translation unit: declare `typedef struct order order;` in the header and define the struct only in order.c, then route every mutation through order_* functions that validate first and return a status code. The parts are owned by the root (owned pointer plus count, released by order_destroy), and because there is no repository abstraction the whole-cluster load/save is hand-written SQL inside the same module. The classic structure is not replaced but renamed: root = opaque handle, methods = functions taking that handle, invariant = the precondition every mutating function checks.
pitfalls: Nothing stops another .c file from including the private definition and mutating the struct: keep the struct definition inside the implementation translation unit (the rule MISRA C Dir 4.8 exists for) and review any header that exposes it.

Ownership is manual: copying a caller-owned buffer into the aggregate without duplicating it leaves the caller able to mutate internal state, and every removed line must be freed exactly once in order_remove_line and order_destroy.
Incomplete types only stop direct member access, not mutation through a casted or duplicated pointer; never expose sizeof or a stack copy of the struct to callers.
There is no unit of work: order_save must write the root and all lines in one transaction, otherwise a crash leaves a half-persisted cluster.
